name: the-events-calendar
notes: The exact supported free-plugin boundary is official WordPress.org The Events Calendar 6.17.2 (SHA-256 f67f2668fc777505a6e0f2cc8c7c39db869a1b186b2444f9d5e138d32bcaabaa) and 6.17.3 (SHA-256 2db436c929797bfc5311be942158c474716e61c2f289f7d05c3a08d29b2ad687), expressed as >=6.17.2 <6.17.4. Certified evidence binds both exact artifacts, the populated 6.17.2-to-6.17.3 upgrade, the official adjacent 6.17.1 refusal, and the exclusive synthetic 6.17.4 refusal; widening requires a new source, schema, regenerator, lifecycle, and native-behavior audit.

Grind R3-B (task #91). Real schema verified live on The Events Calendar 6.17.2 (free, wp.org slug `the-events-calendar`) — every table/option/meta-key claim below was empirically checked (SHOW TABLES, DESCRIBE, create real content and SELECT before/after, read plugin source), not carried over from the task brief's own shorthand, which turned out to be wrong on one point: there are NO `tribe_*` custom tables at all (SHOW TABLES LIKE 'wp_tribe\_%' returns zero rows) — venues (`tribe_venue`) and organizers (`tribe_organizer`) are plain CPTs, exactly as expected, referenced from an event's postmeta via `_EventVenueID`/`_EventOrganizerID` (both `ref: post`, generic post refs — the ref system is keyed by entity kind, not specific post_type, same as `_thumbnail_id`). Recurring events are an Events Calendar PRO (paid) feature: free TEC's own `Single_Event_Migration_Strategy::__construct()` (see the tec_events/tec_occurrences note below) explicitly throws 'Attempting to run Single Event strategy for recurring event. Install and activate the latest version of Events Calendar PRO' the moment `_EventRecurrence` postmeta carries any `rules` — confirmed by reading the source, not by installing Pro to test it; free TEC simply never writes that meta key, so the boundary is enforced by the plugin's own absence of the feature, not by anything Duo does.

tec_events / tec_occurrences (the central finding of this round — DERIVED, but with a HARD query-availability dependency, not a soft cache): TEC 6.x's 'Custom Tables v1' architecture maintains two custom tables alongside the classic `_Event*` postmeta, populated automatically the moment a `tribe_events` post is created via the repository (`tribe_events()->set_args([...])->create()`) — verified live: creating one event instantly produced matching rows in both `tec_events` (event_id PK, post_id UNIQUE, start/end dates, timezone, duration, hash) and `tec_occurrences` (occurrence_id PK, event_id + post_id FK-shaped columns, its own start/end dates, a UNIQUE hash) with byte-identical date values to the classic postmeta. The FIRST empirical test (per task #91's own suggestion) was deleting both rows for a throwaway event and checking whether TEC's own machinery rebuilds them — it does NOT self-heal on any WordPress-native trigger: neither an ordinary `wp post update` resave (fires `save_post`, TEC does not hook table regeneration to it) NOR TEC's own repository query (`tribe_events()->where('id', $id)->first()`) could find the post afterward. The second, sharper test: `wp post list --post_type=tribe_events` — a PLAIN WP_Query, nothing TEC-view-specific — returned ZERO rows for a post independently confirmed (via `wp post get`) to still exist with `post_type=tribe_events`. TEC's `WP_Query\Provider` filters query SQL for this post type to require a matching `tec_occurrences` row; without one, the post is not merely poorly-rendered on a calendar view, it is INVISIBLE to WP_Query itself, admin post list included. This is a materially harder dependency than any derived custom table this project has classified before (nf3_upgrades' stale-cache and wc_product_meta_lookup's query-optimization role are both soft — the owning post/row remains fully findable either way). A REAL regeneration path exists and was verified working: TEC ships `TEC\Events\Custom_Tables\V1\Migration\Strategies\Single_Event_Migration_Strategy`, built for exactly this recovery scenario (upgrading a pre-6.0 site, whose events predate these tables, is a first-class supported case) — its two operative calls, `Event::upsert(['post_id'], Event::data_from_post($post_id))` then `Event::find($post_id, 'post_id')->occurrences()->save_occurrences()`, read straight from the post's own postmeta (bypassing the broken occurrence-dependent query path entirely) and were confirmed live to fully restore both tables and re-establish `wp post list` visibility for the same post.

tec_events and tec_occurrences remain derived rather than authored because every deterministic field is reconstructed from the event post and its owned metadata. The explicit per-event `regen_dependency` now supplies the missing hard query-availability postcondition: it preflights exact table/index/engine, native service, hook, cache, transaction, and source-row topology; locks the source and both derived owner ranges; invokes the reviewed free-plugin path; and verifies every deterministic row field before apply may advance. Schema, binding, hook, cache, transaction, cardinality, linkage, or witness drift refuses instead of falling back to a generic command or copying derived rows.

The historical fresh-target invisibility defect is not an accepted manual step. The batch regenerator runs for every written event, retains durable retry authority after a partial or ambiguous failure, and requires exact Custom Tables V1 readback plus native query visibility before success. Exact-boundary production evidence exercises that behavior together with rollback/retry, concurrency, and lifecycle recovery on both supported plugin artifacts.

DUO-3234 plus the 2026-08-22 production-readiness stale-row regression: `post_types.tribe_events.regen_dependency` declares an always-on-write refresh, because row existence is insufficient — an adopted target event can already have Custom Tables V1 rows whose values or linkage disagree with the applied post meta. `regenerator: "the-events-calendar"` resolves to `manifests/regenerators/the-events-calendar.php`, which wraps the exact two verified-live calls this note already named (`Event::upsert()` + `Event::find()->occurrences()->save_occurrences()`), re-confirmed against the real TEC 6.17.2/6.17.3 source (src/Events/Custom_Tables/V1/Migration/Strategies/Single_Event_Migration_Strategy.php:70-107) before being wrapped. Readback requires exactly one related tec_events row and one free-plugin occurrence, compares every deterministic post/date/UTC/timezone/duration/hash/link field, validates only the generated IDs/timestamps rather than copying them, and rejects partial, duplicate, wrong-link, orphan, query-error, and filter-corrupted outcomes without exposing authored values. Empty `_EventDuration` follows the plugin's exact UTC-endpoint fallback. `verify: {table: "tec_occurrences", column: "post_id"}` remains the generic existence backstop. tec_events/tec_occurrences themselves stay derived and excluded from capture — this declaration changes only the target postcondition.

tec_kv_cache: a generic key/value cache table (cache_key PK, value, expiration) — confirmed by DESCRIBE and by its own name; holds zero site-builder content by construction. Classified runtime (a cache, not a per-entity query-availability dependency like tec_events/tec_occurrences — losing it just means TEC recomputes whatever it cached).

tribe_events_calendar_options is a mixed parent option: the parent stays environment-owned while the reviewed closed `sub_keys` inventory separates portable presentation/editor/SEO settings from schema, cache, cleaner, import, integration, consent, and credential state. In particular, `google_maps_js_api_key` and the Event Aggregator credentials never enter canonical state. The native writer bypasses WordPress option hooks only after binding the exact 6.17.2/6.17.3 listener and filter topology; it then transactionally reproduces the Settings Manager request-cache value, both CacheListener timestamp rows in callback-registration order, their exact autoload transitions, and the request-local transient-purge flag. Unknown callbacks, substituted same-class services, companion drift, partial writes, cache failure and local restoration failure all refuse with exact DB rollback and same-process retry authority. Certified exact-boundary evidence proves this contract together with every readiness family.

Views V2 Customizer capture preserves the native canonical-versus-legacy precedence as storage intent, not only as an effective value: absent `tribe_customizer` plus absent or empty target-owned `tribe_events_pro_customizer` emits canonical absence; a physically present empty canonical row emits explicit present-empty intent; and a nonempty legacy-only source is normalized into the canonical authored record with the declared first-save autoload. Apply locks the target legacy row/gap as an exact companion and never mutates it. Repository state compiled before this corrected adapter identity could contain a manufactured PRESENT empty canonical record with no recoverable source-absence provenance; it must be recaptured/recompiled under the new digest rather than silently reinterpreted.

tec_ct1_events_table_schema_version / tec_ct1_migration_state / tec_ct1_occurrences_table_schema_version / tec_timed_tec_custom_tables_v1_initialized: env — Custom Tables v1's own schema-version and one-time-migration bookkeeping, directly related to the tec_events/tec_occurrences finding above (these are what TEC reads to decide whether the custom-tables migration has already run on THIS environment) but themselves plain env-local markers, not content.

stellar_schema_version_stellarwp-shepherd-tec-tasks / stellar_schema_version_tec-kv-cache: env — StellarWP (TEC's parent company) shared-library schema-version markers for the background-job ('Shepherd') and kv-cache subsystems; same species as woocommerce_db_version.

stellarwp_telemetry / stellarwp_telemetry_last_send / stellarwp_telemetry_the-events-calendar_show_optin: runtime — telemetry opt-in state and send-timestamp bookkeeping, auto-managed, never site-builder-authored config.
tribe_last_generate_rewrite_rules / tribe_last_save_post / tribe_last_updated_option: runtime — internal cache-invalidation timestamps (when various caches were last rebuilt), not content.

_EventShowMap / _EventShowMapLink: declared lint_ok true, reactively, after `wp duo lint` actually flagged both on this round's own 3-event fixture (matches=post:1 'Hello world!') — both are boolean 0/1 display-toggle flags TEC sets on every event by default; reviewed and confirmed genuinely not refs, the same escape hatch as manifests/ninja-forms.json's BIT(1) columns and manifests/woocommerce.json's `queryId`.

_EventOrigin / _OrganizerOrigin / _VenueOrigin: a plain string TEC stamps on every event/venue/organizer it creates ('events-calendar') identifying the creation source (vs. an import from another calendar system) — static per-entity provenance, not env-bound, not a ref: authored.

post_meta absent entirely when unset, not written empty: confirmed live — an event created with no venue/organizer (this round's 'Community Meetup' fixture) carries ZERO `_EventVenueID`/`_EventOrganizerID` postmeta rows, not empty-string rows, matching the ordinary WordPress 'absent key = unset ref' convention the engine's ref-token machinery already assumes.

Version window widened 2026-08-24 from the one-release >=6.17.2 <6.17.3 to >=6.17.2 <6.17.4, on evidence, not on inertia: 6.17.3 (official wp.org artifact, SHA-256 2db436c929797bfc5311be942158c474716e61c2f289f7d05c3a08d29b2ad687) is the only release upstream has published above the previously inspected 6.17.2 artifact. The adapter surface was probed the same way manifests/code-snippets.json probed class-db.php before widening ITS window: src/Events/Custom_Tables/V1/** is byte-identical across the two artifacts, Single_Event_Migration_Strategy.php (the file the tec_events/tec_occurrences note above cites at :70-100, and the exact path manifests/regenerators/the-events-calendar.php wraps) hashes to f307a323aecb78f3004abea04d002e78d1a90d417baa7c6c22f3796db4cf3c12 in both, and Events::SCHEMA_VERSION/Occurrences::SCHEMA_VERSION stay 1.0.1/1.0.3 -- so both env-class schema-version options this manifest declares resolve unchanged. The non-translation, non-changelog deltas are src/Tribe/Views/V2/{Url,View,Template/Title,Widgets/Service_Provider}.php. The widget provider is state-bearing, not merely front-end rendering: its core/legacy-widget copy, save, and render callbacks decode a base64 PHP-serialized instance and re-sign it with wp_hash(), and 6.17.3 newly rejects nested objects after unserializing with allowed_classes=false. Normal stored-id blocks also address sidebars_widgets plus widget_<idBase> through SidebarState. The manifest-bound codec now validates and rebases both exact forms, discards source hashes, re-signs bounded plain instances with the target salt, and keeps every non-TEC legacy widget outside the adapter contract. Exact source evidence is in the TEC option-hook fixture/verifier. Exercised at both edges by sandbox/tests/certify/certify_version_matrix.sh (VMATRIX_MANIFEST=the-events-calendar), including a populated 6.17.2 -> 6.17.3 in-place upgrade that must refuse as code_drift, redeploy under --force-code-drift, and then produce an empty plan in all seven buckets. Widening past 6.17.4 requires the same probe against the next artifact.

The 6.17.2/6.17.3 source audit supersedes historical one-artifact assumptions. Their Custom Tables v1 implementation is byte-identical and the exclusive 6.17.4 maximum cannot silently admit a future release. Production evidence binds both exact boundaries, a populated 6.17.2-to-6.17.3 in-place upgrade, the official 6.17.1 adjacent refusal, and the synthetic exclusive-upper refusal to one clean certified adapter identity.

tribe_events_calendar_options remains environment-owned as a whole, while the reviewed sub_keys below enumerate the free plugin's stable human-authored presentation, editor, SEO, category-color, and timezone settings. Credentials, Event Aggregator remote-import state, event-cleaner schedules, schema/version markers, telemetry, date-range caches, legacy linked-post inputs, and explicitly named bundled integration keys remain target-owned. Production promotion is blocked until `closed_sub_keys` makes that inventory authoritative and refuses an unknown populated sibling at both capture and apply.

TEC 6.17.2/6.17.3 free ships Category Colors as a native feature. tribe_events_cat and its five exact tec-events-cat-colors-* term-meta keys are authored state; the interpreter rejects malformed colors, priorities, and flags before compilation. Events Calendar Pro recurrence, Event Tickets state, Event Aggregator records and credentials, legacy Category Colors plugin residue, third-party add-ons, and multisite remain outside this contract and refuse rather than receiving inferred authority.

Event, venue, organizer, and event-category deletion remain deliberately unsupported. Duo's generic entity deletion is hook-free while TEC and optional add-ons own occurrence cleanup, Category Colors effects, and reverse-reference behavior; the batch regenerator refuses deletion context before mutation, and exact conformance fingerprints the complete physical surface around each refusal so no tombstone or partial target change can be certified.

Exact 6.17.2/6.17.3 source and native conformance expose a second hard derived-state path in bundled Category Colors. Event_Category_Meta::save() writes only five authored term-meta values; Duo therefore invokes the exact Generator then dropdown-cache bust services in the reviewed Controller order while refusing container overrides, external caches, output filters, and Options-API hook drift. Invocation requires the cache entry absent after the native bust. Read-only reconciliation never calls get_dropdown_categories(): it observes the raw native cache and accepts only absence or one bounded populated value whose normalized rows exactly match the current category/color projection; stale, malformed, unreadable, or foreign rows refuse, while natural expiry and legitimate repopulation do not create false debt. CSS verification rejects extra selectors, recognized declarations, duplicates, comments, and filter output while treating equal-priority selector order as semantically commutative. The native unordered LIMIT/OFFSET scan is admitted through one complete 500-row page only; 501 relevant rows refuse before mutation. The derived CSS option remains excluded from capture, and both its durable option effect and native dropdown-cache effect are declared explicitly.

Free TEC 6.17.2/6.17.3 registers `_EventOrganizerID` as non-single numeric metadata and its native APIs/templates preserve multiple unique organizer rows in physical order. The manifest declares the reviewed repeated-row grammar: one canonical post token per row, unique and order-preserving, with exact row replacement on apply. The merged shared platform supplies its bounded physical reader, owner-range lock, transaction and post-meta cache seam. TEC's deterministic product path now exercises divergent large-ID capture/rebase, empty/one/many replacement, physical order, stale-row deletion, cache invalidation, no-op retry, canonical recapture, duplicate/empty refusal, injected insertion rollback/retry, same-count same-length terminal drift, and zero-row deletion. Production promotion remains blocked on exact raw-row, REST, block and frontend evidence for both artifacts. Event status is stored only as paired `_tribe_events_status`/`_tribe_events_status_reason` rows for canceled or postponed events; scheduled is native absence. Preview linked-post lists are editor-runtime cleanup state. Debug, month-view cache, past-event trash/delete settings, credentials, imports, and cleaner scheduling remain target-owned because direct sub-key writes would bypass their operational hooks.

Exact-source and native-path audit found that current free TEC intentionally reaches multiple physical boolean wires. Registered Gutenberg `_EventAllDay` writes `1`/empty while the public classic API writes `yes`/`no`, and repository creation may use `yes` or absence depending on request context. `_EventHideFromUpcoming` uses `yes`/absence through the repository and classic editor, while the documented bool-typed public helper writes `1`/empty. The interpreter admits only those exact string wires; malformed aliases and typed values refuse. Conformance crosses hostile classic `yes` rows into registered `1`/empty state, deletes stale truthy rows where the source is absent, and verifies native all-day and hidden-event readers.

Free TEC 6.17.2/6.17.3's registered `tribe/event-organizer` block stores one local organizer post ID in its scalar `organizer` attribute; its separate `organizers` attribute is sourced from `_EventOrganizerID` and is not serialized into post content. The block rule rebases each populated organizer instance independently. The interpreter permits classic content with no organizer blocks and Gutenberg's empty placeholder, but populated organizer blocks must carry unique ordered canonical tokens exactly matching the repeated `_EventOrganizerID` rows. A block nested under a Group is intentionally inspected and accepted only when that invariant holds; TEC's supplemental reorder scan is top-level-only, and exact live evidence proves nested capture/apply/recapture coherence. The organizer block itself may not contain inner blocks or authored inner HTML. Raw or huge local IDs, wrong post types, duplicate/reordered/malformed attributes, and persisted meta-sourced lists refuse before deploy.

The exact free 6.17.2 and 6.17.3 Settings Manager call inventories are identical (sorted literal-key inventory SHA-256 ba1fa249f2f188946e5577046ffa91a0c67a57bdddc91fcefaeb34427295a9a9). The registry also includes computed property/constant writers that a literal-call scan cannot see: cleaner and REST flags, all three schema updaters, first-boot and activation markers, seven fixed Aggregator origins, timed-option names, CSV mappings, Category Colors migrations, and exact Event Automator endpoint/connection names. Legacy aliases that still affect free rendering are authored; cache/version/credential/consent/import/extension state is explicitly target-owned. Shared `fs_active_plugins`, classic-editor options, Common timed-option extensions, and third-party namespace additions are not claimed by this adapter.

Exact-source ownership correction: free 6.17.2/6.17.3 exposes no settings registration or authoring path for `custom-fields`, `allow_duplicate_venues`, `eventsDefaultVenueID`, `eventsDefaultOrganizerID`, `geoloc_default_unit`, `liveFiltersUpdate`, or `tribeEventsCountries`. They are extension/legacy inputs: `custom-fields` is the Pro field registry, Filter Bar or other add-ons may inject live-filter/geolocation settings, and the free Default_Values strategy returns no linked-post defaults. Free Amalgamator only repoints a pre-existing default ID while merging duplicates; that cleanup is not a free default-selection surface. These keys remain explicitly target-owned, carry no free-plugin reference or arbitrary plain-data claim, and cannot leak licensed configuration into a free adapter.

`front_page_event_archive` is not independently authored: Front_Page_View::save_page_on_front() derives it from WordPress `page_on_front`, using TEC's virtual post ID -10. Core correctly treats ordinary positive `page_on_front` as a post reference, but -10 has no portable post identity. The TEC mirror therefore remains target runtime state, and an enabled source pair must refuse loudly rather than capture one half or invent a post token; disabled and ordinary positive-page homepage states remain within their owning core contracts.
